comparator.sourceNotes: This 180 EC example follows the German major language and European Language and Society profile in the 2026–2027 regulations. It includes all three first German-specific modules, the later interdisciplinary German module, 10 EC of restricted electives, a 30 EC minor and a 10 EC thesis.

questionsApplications.label: How do language, media and communication shape identity and power in European societies?
How do literature and cultural expression represent similarities and differences across Europe?
How have political institutions and social change shaped modern Europe and its future challenges?

alternatives.concept: Study how language works and how it shapes public life. Begin with everyday Dutch, rhetoric and the study of language and thought. Apply those perspectives to literary texts, media and social debates, with modern European history and EU politics as regional anchors.
basisLabels: Language proficiency, language-and-society analysis, multilingual communication and language-specific academic work
European cultures, identities, literature, text, media and comparative cultural analysis
European politics, institutions, social change and contemporary challenges
How do language, media and communication shape identity and power in European societies?
alternatives.labelRationale: Dutch, stylistics, psycholinguistics and rhetoric lead the route. Modern History and European Union Politics provide European context alongside wider cultural and social comparisons.

alternatives.concept: Follow stories and images across literature, film and visual art. Move from close reading and Renaissance art to adaptation, documentary and the history of art interpretation. Use these methods to examine how identity and power are represented across societies.
basisLabels: Language proficiency, language-and-society analysis, multilingual communication and language-specific academic work
European cultures, identities, literature, text, media and comparative cultural analysis
European politics, institutions, social change and contemporary challenges
How do literature and cultural expression represent similarities and differences across Europe?
alternatives.labelRationale: The route progresses from literary and visual interpretation to research on narratives, film and art. The Italian Renaissance and European documentary traditions add regional examples within a wider cultural comparison.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The literature and media and the language and society options differ by 52.5 EC each way. Literary history and criticism, myth, visual art and adaptation take the place of Dutch, psycholinguistics, EU politics and several social science courses.

alternatives.concept: Study modern Europe through history, political institutions and conflict. Build from political philosophy and comparative politics to EU decision-making, international relations and research on social change. Use media and literature to explore how public debates take shape.
basisLabels: European cultures, identities, literature, text, media and comparative cultural analysis
European politics, institutions, social change and contemporary challenges
How have political institutions and social change shaped modern Europe and its future challenges?
alternatives.labelRationale: Modern history, European Union Politics and comparative politics anchor the route. Historical and qualitative inquiry, peace studies and social theory support the study of political and social change.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The politics option differs by 75 EC from the language option and 75 EC from the literature option in each direction. Its distinctive core is political philosophy, comparative politics, international relations, historical research and conflict.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three coherent schedules cover the main interests through language and society, literature and cultural identity, and politics and social change. Each pair differs by at least 30 EC in each direction. The separate proficiency direction has insufficient language instruction across all eight languages.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both examine linguistic structure, including word and sentence patterns. UCR applies this to meaning in texts, while Groningen compares the structures of European languages.
Both study how the mind processes language. Groningen focuses on psycho- and neurolinguistic research methods.
Both analyse how stories shape identity. UCR focuses on memoir, autobiography and travel writing.
Both interpret and produce narratives. UCR works in the specific form of nonfiction film.
Both introduce the interpretation of literature. Groningen places texts in a European cultural context.
Both examine modern European history. Groningen also introduces linguistic and political ways to study Europe.
Both examine democracy and political institutions. UCR uses a wider comparative scope.
The first German Plus course develops comprehension and communication at intermediate level.
Groningen introduces European language and society as a dedicated field.
Groningen continues the German sequence through formal written and spoken communication.
Groningen develops academic skills in the context of the programme profiles.
The third German course develops academic communication at C1.
Groningen reserves 10 EC for a choice within the programme’s profile and language options.
Groningen applies linguistic analysis to Standard German.
Groningen examines first- and second-language learning through theory and research.
Groningen analyses literary genres and periods in German.
Groningen studies German political culture and its European context in the major language.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for a minor or approved study abroad.
This advanced German module brings together linguistics, literature and politics.
Groningen teaches linguistic research design, corpus or questionnaire work and basic statistical analysis.
Groningen requires a 10 EC thesis. The optional UCR research shown alongside it is separate from the course schedules.

notes.text: Groningen combines a three-course German proficiency sequence with academic study in German. The UCR options offer introductory Dutch, linguistics, literature, media or European politics in different combinations.
The UCR course options do not include a German proficiency sequence or the specialist modules taught in German. Groningen’s minor and required thesis are shown separately in the curriculum.

audience.programmeDescription: Groningen’s degree combines study of a major European language with questions about language, literature and politics. The example shown follows German and the European Language and Society profile.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options focus on language and society, literature and media, or modern European politics. The Groningen example includes advanced language study in German.

curriculum.routeLabel: German major language, European Language and Society profile

cellNotes.text: Both examine linguistic structure, including word and sentence patterns. UCR applies this to meaning in texts, while Groningen compares the structures of European languages.
Both study how the mind processes language. Groningen focuses on psycho- and neurolinguistic research methods.
Both interpret and produce narratives. UCR works in the specific form of nonfiction film.
Both analyse how stories shape identity. UCR focuses on memoir, autobiography and travel writing.
Both introduce the interpretation of literature. Groningen places texts in a European cultural context.
Both examine modern European history. Groningen also introduces linguistic and political ways to study Europe.
Both examine democracy and political institutions. UCR uses a wider comparative scope.
The first German Plus course develops comprehension and communication at intermediate level.
Groningen introduces European language and society as a dedicated field.
Groningen continues the German sequence through formal written and spoken communication.
Groningen develops academic skills in the context of the programme profiles.
The third German course develops academic communication at C1.
Groningen reserves 10 EC for a choice within the programme’s profile and language options.
Groningen applies linguistic analysis to Standard German.
Groningen examines first- and second-language learning through theory and research.
Groningen analyses literary genres and periods in German.
Groningen studies German political culture and its European context in the major language.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for a minor or approved study abroad.
This advanced German module brings together linguistics, literature and politics.
Groningen teaches linguistic research design, corpus or questionnaire work and basic statistical analysis.
Groningen requires a 10 EC thesis. The optional UCR research shown alongside it is separate from the course schedules.
